messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed in our galaxy is the protoplanet **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and is still forming; its radius is estimated at roughly **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter** (about 0.25 R☉).  Because it is a protoplanet, its mass is not yet precisely measured, but it is clearly the biggest “planet‑size” object we have found so far.

> **Key points**  
> • HD 100546 b is a *protoplanet*—a planet in the process of forming.  
> • Its radius (~2.5 R_J) makes it larger than any other confirmed exoplanet.  
> • It is located about 350 light‑years from Earth in the constellation Musca.  

If you’re interested in the most massive exoplanets (in terms of mass rather than size), those are typically “hot Jupiters” or brown dwarfs with masses up to a few tens of Jupiter masses, but they are usually smaller in radius than HD 100546 b.
